title: De lineis curvis non in eodem plano sitis, quae maximi minimive proprietate sunt praeditae

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E740 looks for space curves that extremize a functional depending on the distance v = sqrt(x²+y²+z²) from a fixed centre and on the arc element s dx, where s = sqrt(1+p²+q²), p = dy/dx, q = dz/dx. The previous page reduced the Euler–Lagrange system to two second-order equations: (I) y dx − x dy = v² dp/s² and (II) z dx − x dz = v² dq/s². The next page shows the planar extremals are rectangular hyperbolas centred at the origin, which points to the functional ∫ v ds. This identification is my inference: in polar coordinates the extremals of ∫ r^k ds satisfy r^{k+1} cos((k+1)θ) = const, and k = 1 gives r² cos 2θ = const.

Planarity. Dividing (I) by (II) gave dp/(y−px) = dq/(z−qx). Since d(y−px) = −x dp, this integrates to z − qx = n(y−px). In modern terms, (y−px, z−qx) are two components of r × r', so this is a first integral for the rotational symmetry. Then d(z−qx) = n d(y−px) gives −x dq = −n x dp, so dq = n dp and q = np + a. Integrating gives z = ny + ax + b. Substituting back into z − qx = n(y−px) forces b = 0. Hence the extremal lies in a plane through the centre, which is what one expects from rotational invariance.

Reduction in the plane. Put z = ny + ax. Then v² = x²+y²+(ny+ax)² and s² = 1+p²+(np+a)², and (I) becomes (y dx − x dy)/v² = dp/s². With y = ux we have y dx − x dy = −x² du and v² = x²(1+u²+(nu+a)²). The equation becomes the separated form −du/(1+u²+(nu+a)²) = dp/(1+p²+(np+a)²), whose two sides have identical form.

Integration step. Expand s² = (1+n²)(p² + 2αp + β) with α = an/(1+n²) and β = (1+a²)/(1+n²), then substitute t = p + α. The next page integrates each side as an arctan with the same coefficient, so the sum of the two arctangents is constant. Taking the tangent of the sum gives an algebraic relation (1+n²)pu − a² − 1 = f((1+n²)(p+u) + 2an). Since p = dy/dx and u = y/x, this is a first-order equation solvable by dx/x = du/(p−u).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. All substitutions check: −x² du / (x²(1+u²+(nu+a)²)); α = an/(1+nn); β = (1+aa)/(1+nn); β − α² = (1+a²+n²)/(1+n²)² > 0, so the arctangent form on the next page is legitimate.
Minor presentational point: Euler first writes z = ny + ax + b and only afterwards notes b = 0. The two steps are consistent.

ideas.what: Ratio of two 'angular-momentum' components (y−px, z−qx) is constant, which forces the extremal into a plane through the centre (b = 0)
ideas.modern_name: First integrals from rotational symmetry (Noether-type conservation); planarity of extremals of centrally symmetric functionals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical: Euler and Lagrange (central-force motion is planar); general symmetry principle due to Noether (1918)
ideas.where_published: Planarity of central-force orbits is standard in Euler's mechanics (Mechanica 1736 and later papers). This variational space-curve version is E740 itself.

ideas.what: Reduction of the planar equation to a separated equation with identical sides in u = y/x and p = dy/dx
ideas.modern_name: In polar terms, polar angle plus a weighted tangent angle is constant: the integration of extremals of ∫ r ds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (planar extremals of ∫ r^n ds are treated in Methodus inveniendi, 1744)
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas (E65) for planar central functionals; E740 for the spatial version

ideas.what: Integration via addition of two arctangents with equal coefficients, giving an algebraic relation between p and u
ideas.modern_name: Arctangent addition formula used as an integration device

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine but neat steps: a symmetry-derived first integral forces planarity, followed by a reduction to a separated equation. Both the results (planar extremals; rectangular hyperbolas for ∫ v ds) and the methods are classical and appear in Euler's own published work. Nothing appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In §28 the denominator should read 1 + aa + 2anp + (nn+1)pp; the '+' before (nn+1)pp is missing in the transcription.
In the separated equation the numerator of the left side is −∂u, not −∂x; the scan shows ∂u, consistent with y = ux.
